chapter: Meeting Louis and the New Orleans bands
title: Losing a trumpet and sleeping with the second one
summary: Keys on his trumpet were ruined and the horn was lost; he paid for a replacement and jokes about keeping it in bed with him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yeah. I guess you're scared of it, huh? Well, you just went in there. Did you borrow an instrument that time?
No, I had my instrument in my hand. I stole it out there on me. Put it in my bag. And I looked down there and put it in my bag.
Did you always carry it with you? When you went to the different-

Well, I played it long until they filled out the keys one day, one night at least. Straight on the upper line of the street, I think it was. And the keys didn't lock good, and I forgot about it. They dropped in a barrel, and they weren't there with no more good. So I carried it to the phone shelf, and I jived them by the way I just played on the two valves, and they're talking, give me fifteen dollars. So that's what I just got to come with that one. But I got another one right away, huh?
Did you sleep with your trumpet? Yeah.
You wouldn't let it out of your-
Except that trumpet. You didn't really sleep with your trumpet, did you? In the bed?
Yeah. I had to. I had no case with the second one I got. Yeah, the second one.
And you didn't have any case? And you actually would put it in bed with?
Put it right down in the pillow, man. I was kidding.
